entry.title: Conductivity of a non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid: Exact solution of the kinetic equation
entry.summary:
Author(s): Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, and Dmitrii L. Maslov In a Fermi liquid, the quasiparticle scattering rate scales as T2, whereas the low-temperature correction to the residual resistivity can scale as T4, seemingly implying a strongly suppressed current-relaxation rate. The authors resolve this paradox here by solving the kinetic equation exactly for a disordered, non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid. They show that electron–electron collisions enter the conductivity through the quasiparticle scattering time itself, which controls the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic transport. The extra T2 factor arises because momentum conservation makes the change in the total velocity of two colliding electrons vanish on the Fermi surface, so current relaxation comes only from thermally excited states away from it. The electron–electron contribution to the dc conductivity nevertheless remains parametrically small throughout the Fermi-liquid regime. By extrapolating the result toward a z=3 quantum critical point, the authors further show that the renormalized quasiparticle scattering rate saturates the Planckian bound.
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L291103] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026

entry.title: Delivery of refractory radioactive ion beams via in-trap decay at ISOLDE

Author(s): J. R. Reilly, M. Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis, M. Au, L. Nies, A. Ajayakumar, M. Benhatchi, J. Berbalk, C. Bernerd, K. Chrysalidis, C. M. Fajardo Zambrano, P. F. Giesel, R. Heinke, D. Lange, G. Peng, S. Rothe, A. Schmidt, C. Schweiger, and J. Wessolek The delivery of radioactive ion beams of refractory elements using the ISOL method remains challenging, limiting access to isotopes for nuclear-structure studies. We demonstrate a method to overcome this limitation using in-trap β− decay in the ISCOOL radiofrequency quadrupole trap at CERN-ISOLDE. Radioactive parent ions are confined in helium buffer gas, where their decay products can be slowed, captured and extracted as an ion beam. Using 97,98Rb and 98Sr, we produce 97,98Sr and 98Y, monitoring their populations as a function of trapping time with the ISOLTRAP multi-reflection time-of-flight mass spectrometer. Fits to Bateman decay equations reproduce the known half-lives, validating the method and demonstrating daughter-beam efficiencies of approximately 1% relative to the initial parent intensity. We report the first delivery of a singly charged atomic 98Y beam at ISOLDE. This approach requires no modification to the existing target or ion source and opens new opportunities to study refractory isotopes that are otherwise difficult to extract.
[Phys. Rev. C 114, 054311] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026

Here, the authors investigate superconductivity in σ-phase Re–X (X = V, Nb, and Ta) alloys, covering 3d, 4d, and 5d transition-metal substitutions, as well as in a derived medium-entropy alloy incorporating multiple transition metals.
